source_text: Quam unitatem tenere firmiter et uindicare debemus, maxime episcopi qui in ecclesia praesidemus, ut episcopatum quoque ipsum unum adque indiuisum probemus. nemo fraternitatem mendacio fallat, nemo fidem ueritatis perfida praeuaricatione corrumpat. episcopatus unus est, cuius a singulis in solidum pars tenetur. ecclesia una est quae in multitudinem latius incremento fecunditatis extenditur, quomodo solis multi radii sed lumen unum, et rami arboris multi sed robur unum tenaci radice fundatum, et cum de fonte uno riui plurimi defluunt, numerositas licet diffusa uideatur exundantis copiae largitate, unitas tamen seruatur in origine. auelle radium solis a corpore, diuisionem lucis unitas non capit: ab arbore frange ramum, fractus germinare non poterit: a fonte praecide riuum, praecisus arescit. sic et ecclesia Domini luce perfusa per orbem totum radios suos porrigit: unum tamen lumen est quod ubique diffunditur, nec unitas corporis separatur. ramos suos in uniuersam terram copia ubertatis extendit, profluentes largiter riuos latius pandit: unum tamen caput est et origo una et una mater fecunditatis successibus copiosa: illius fetu nascimur, illius lacte nutrimur, spiritu eius animamur.
thought_title: The Church's unity shown by natural images
orientation: Cyprian, bishop of Carthage, is addressing the bishops who preside in the Church, urging them to hold and defend the Church's unity.
pass_a_gloss: This unity we ought to hold firmly and to defend, especially we bishops who preside in the Church, so that we may prove the episcopate itself also to be one and undivided. Let no one deceive the brotherhood with a lie, let no one corrupt the faith of truth by a treacherous violation. The episcopate is one, of which a part is held by individuals in solidum. The Church is one, which is extended into a multitude more widely by the increase of fruitfulness, just as there are many rays of the sun but one light, and many branches of a tree but one strength founded on a tenacious root, and when from one spring many streams flow down, although the numerousness may seem spread out by the abundance of the overflowing plenty, yet unity is preserved in the origin. Tear away a ray of the sun from its body, the unity does not admit a division of the light: break a branch from the tree, the broken branch will not be able to sprout: cut off a stream from the spring, the cut-off stream dries up. So also the Church of the Lord, flooded with light, stretches out its rays through the whole world: yet it is one light that is spread everywhere, nor is the unity of the body separated. It extends its branches into the whole earth by the abundance of its fruitfulness, it spreads out its flowing streams more widely: yet there is one head and one origin and one mother, rich in the successes of fruitfulness: from her offspring we are born, by her milk we are nourished, by her spirit we are given life.

choices.why: Legal term meaning each bishop holds the whole episcopate jointly, not a divided share; kept in Latin to preserve the technical sense.
Conveys the sense of a treacherous breach of faith, matching the perfida adjective.
Glossary-adjacent term for the Church's generative abundance; consistent with the maternal imagery.

choices.english: by the abundance of the overflowing plenty
choices.why: Keeps the double emphasis on overflowing and abundance, matching the rhetorical fullness of the Latin.
rejected: by the generosity of the overflowing supply
by the lavishness of the overflowing abundance

choices.why: Renders the concrete sense of successive births or offspring, fitting the maternal image.

pass_b_english: We must hold firmly to this unity and defend it, especially we bishops who preside in the Church, so that we may prove that the episcopate itself is also one and undivided. Let no one deceive the brotherhood with a lie; let no one corrupt the faith of truth by a treacherous violation. The episcopate is one, and each bishop holds his part in solidum. The Church is one, yet she extends into a multitude more widely by the increase of her fruitfulness. Just as there are many rays of the sun but one light, and many branches of a tree but one trunk grounded in a tenacious root, and just as many streams flow from one spring—though the number seems spread out by the abundance of the overflowing plenty, unity is still preserved in the source—so it is with the Church. Tear a ray from the body of the sun: the unity of the light does not admit a division of its light. Break a branch from the tree: once broken, it will not be able to sprout. Cut a stream from the spring: once cut, it dries up. In the same way, the Church of the Lord, flooded with light, stretches out her rays through the whole world. Yet there is one light that is poured out everywhere, and the unity of the body is not separated. She extends her branches over the whole earth in the abundance of her richness, and spreads her flowing streams far and wide. Yet there is one head and one source and one mother, rich in the successes of her fruitfulness. From her womb we are born; by her milk we are nourished; by her Spirit we are given life.
